sections.heading: Explanatory notes
sections.html:
1. Word order

Word order: entries are arranged in dictionary order. Nouns with the same meaning are grouped together, separated by commas, and each also appears in turn under its own letter section. The classifier is shown in the right-hand column, for example:

กงกระสุน (pellet bow) – คัน (khan)
กงเกวียน, กงล้อ (cartwheel, wheel) – กง, วง (kong, wong)

.................................................................................

กรอบเช็ดหน้า, เช็ดหน้า, วงกบ (door or window frame) - วง (wong)

.................................................................................

เช็ดหน้า, กรอบเช๊ดหน้า, วงกบ (door or window frame) - วง (wong)

.................................................................................

วงกบ, กรอบเช็ดหน้า, วงกบ (door or window frame) - วง (wong)

2. Nouns with several meanings

2.1 When assigning classifiers to a noun with several meanings: if every meaning takes the same classifier, no definition is given; if the classifiers differ, a short definition is given in parentheses after the noun to show that only the meaning stated in the parentheses takes the classifier given, for example:

ดารา (star) – ดวง (duang)
……………………………………………………………
ตอม่อ (house post) – ต้น (ton)
ตอม่อ (bridge pier) – ตอม่อ (tomo)

2.2 Nouns with similar or related meanings that take the same classifier are grouped together, separated by semicolons, for example:

ศาล; ศาลเจ้า; ศาลเทพารักษ์ (shrine; Chinese shrine; guardian-spirit shrine) – ศาล (san)

2.3 Nouns with several meanings that take the same classifier are given short definitions in parentheses after the noun, separated by semicolons, for example:

ชนัก (harpoon; elephant neck rope) – เล่ม (lem)

3. Nouns that take several classifiers

Some nouns can take several classifiers. Classifiers are assigned in 3 ways:

3.1 The most commonly used classifier is listed first, followed by the others, separated by commas, for example:

ไข่ (egg) – ใบ, ฟอง, ลูก (bai, fong, luk)
……………………………………………………………
โคม (lamps of various kinds) – ดวง, ใบ, ลูก (duang, bai, luk)

3.2 Different classifiers are assigned according to the item's state, separated by semicolons, to show that although they are classifiers for the same thing, they differ according to its state, for example:

ซิ่น, ผ้าซิ่น (sarong) – ผืน; ตัว, ถุง (phuen; tua, thung)

This means that ซิ่น or ผ้าซิ่น takes the classifier ผืน before it is cut and sewn, but ตัว or ถุง once it has been sewn.

ปิ่นโต (food carrier) – ใบ, ลูก; เถา, สาย (bai, luk; thao, sai)

This means that each individual container of a ปิ่นโต takes the classifier ใบ or ลูก, but when the containers are stacked and held together by a frame, the classifier is เถา or สาย.

Sometimes a short explanation is given in parentheses after the classifier, for example:

ระนาด (xylophone, a pi phat instrument) – ลูก (a single bar); ผืน (a set of bars strung together); ราง (the whole instrument)

3.3 Classifiers are assigned according to size, width, length, quantity, weight or form of use, marked as “named by form” or “named by form or packaging”, followed by example classifiers, for example:

ทอฟฟี่ (toffee) – named by form or packaging, e.g. เม็ด, อัน, ห่อ, แท่ง

Or both a general classifier and packaging-based classifiers are given, for example:

ด้าย (thread) – เส้น; named by form or packaging, e.g. กลุ่ม, เข็ด, ไจ, หลอด

ผม (hair) – เส้น; named by form, e.g. กระจุก, ปอย

4. Collective nouns

For collective nouns such as ขนม (sweets), ผลไม้ (fruit) and ดอกไม้ (flowers), a collective classifier is given without dividing them into subtypes. However, if a subtype takes additional classifiers or classifiers different from the collective ones, the subtype is listed as its own entry with those additional or different classifiers, for example:

ขนม (sweets) – named by form, e.g. ชิ้น, อัน, แผ่น, ตัว;
named by the container, e.g. ถ้วย, ชาม
ขนมครก (coconut pancake) – ฝา; คู่ (fa; khu)
ขนมจีน (Thai rice noodles) – จับ, หัว (chap, hua)
……………………………………………………………
ไข่นกกระสา (a sweet, “stork's egg”) – ลูก (luk)
……………………………………………………………
ซาลาเปา (steamed bun) – ใบ, ลูก (bai, luk)

5. Royal vocabulary nouns

Most of the royal vocabulary terms in this classifier book are words not formed by adding “พระ” before a noun, and are usually used only in connection with the King. Royal terms formed by adding “พระ” before an ordinary noun are included only in small numbers, because most royal vocabulary nouns take the classifier “องค์” unless otherwise specified, for example:

ฉลองพระเนตร (royal spectacles) – องค์ (ong)
ฉลองพระบาท, รองพระบาท (royal shoes) – ข้าง, องค์; คู่ (khang, ong; khu)

Where a noun is both a royal term and an ordinary noun, both classifiers are given, for example:

พระขรรค์ (sacred sword) – องค์ (ong); เล่ม (lem, in general use)
